lawyer:
SS Halder, Senior Advocate instructed by Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioners. 
Not represented—The Respondents.
parties:
Gopal Das Soni and another ------ Petitioners.
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
3. The suit was contested by the defendants averring that the suit is not maintainable and that the land in suit has been recorded in the kash Khatian being within the periphery of the Khulna Hat and Bazar and that the land in suit as per provision of section 20(2a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 is of the class of non-retainable land and that compensation roll in the name of Sree Krishna Soni has already been prepared and the same has been published in the Gazette and that notices were served on Sree Krishna Soni and others. 

 "The Government acquired the land 0.03 acre in CS Khatian No. 295 plot No. 2547 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 367 SA Plot No. 3173 and 0.04 acre in CS Khatian No. 367 Plot No. 2513 corresponding to SA Plot No. 3134 and compensation roll was prepared on 1-9-1962 but the courts below found a rent receipt dated 1-12-1960 which is prior to the compensation assessment roll. The finding that the land is retainable and it is not within the periphery of the Hat and Bazar is contrary to law." ...."Since the property has been acquired by the Government it cannot be the tenanted property of the petitioner. The defendant specifically mentioned in para 8 of their written statement that Sree Krishna Soni died in the year 1963 and it is not denied by the plaintiffs and it is admitted in the Writ Petition No. 394 of 1970. The defendant also made a sketch map of the periphery of the Hat and Bazar. But it was not considered by the appellate Court. It clearly shows that the property is within the periphery of Hat and Bazar of Khulna."
